intro.q: What are fields by standard for?
intro.sub: By assigning catalogue fields to standards, the set of custom fields of every element type can be generated automatically, since each type takes on the custom fields of the standards that apply to it.

intro.q: How are the fields of an element type put together?
intro.sub: The fields of an element type can be composed in three ways:
intro.autoTxt: from the fields by standard. The type takes on the fields of the standard or standards that apply to it.
intro.manualTxt: , by creating fields directly on each type.
intro.mixtoTxt: : taking on all or part of the automatic ones and adding directly created fields.

merge.handle: Drag onto another type to merge them
merge.title: Merge these two element types?
merge.desc: You are about to merge “{{from}}” into “{{to}}”. Both are in the {{familia}} family, so they can be unified into a single type.
merge.normasIguales: Both types declare the same standards ({{normas}}): the merge does not change which standard applies.
merge.normasDistintas: The standards differ. After the merge, those of the type that is kept, “{{to}}”, will apply: {{normas}}. What comes in is no longer governed by {{perdidas}}.
merge.camposPerdidos: Only the custom fields set by “{{to}}” are kept. Those exclusive to “{{from}}” ({{campos}}) disappear, along with the data already recorded in them.
merge.camposIntactos: Only the custom fields set by “{{to}}” are kept. “{{from}}” adds none that “{{to}}” does not have, so no data is lost.
merge.identidadCampo: A field is kept only if it is the same catalogue field in both types. Sharing a name is not enough: renaming a field to match does not merge them.
merge.note: “{{from}}” will cease to exist: its {{n}} items move to “{{to}}” with that type’s configuration (standards, fields and checklists). This cannot be undone.
